text:
Alex (CEO): follow-up from today's all-hands  drop short Qs about mission/positioning/market and we'll answer here.
Jordan (Growth): need a crisp 1-liner for the one-pager vs hyperscalers.
Alex (CEO): "Redwood: production-first inference that makes latency, cost, and portability predictable." keep it tight.
Lina (Sales): Customers ask: why not just use cloud endpoints? what do we say in 20s?
Maya (Head of Product): say: "Clouds offer scale; we offer predictable serving economics and unified ops across hosted/dedicated/private."
Ravi (CTO): tech add-on: mention automatic fallbacks + model variant routing when capacity or cost changes.
Sam (VP Eng): Roadmap point: SLA FAQ + token-cost widgets shipping in 4 weeks, right? can we share dates?
Maya (Head of Product): yes, public FAQ in 3-4 weeks, widget beta in 6 weeks.
Jordan (Growth): competitors question: how blunt should we be comparing feature parity?
Alex (CEO): be factual. call out what we do better (serving economics, developer ergonomics) and where hyperscalers win (global scale, broad infra). keep tone constructive.
Lina (Sales): For trials -> Dedicated path: can users prototype on Hosted then move without heavy rework?
Ravi (CTO): yes  same API surface and model pinning tools; exportable configs. emphasize low-friction migration.
Jordan (Growth): pricing signal: customers with heavy embeddings volume asking for a distinct tier. any updates?
Maya (Head of Product): exploring embeddings compute/storage split + volume discounts. no final rollout yet.
Alex (CEO): important: no surprise price changes for incumbents. any pilot will be opt-in.
Sam (VP Eng): quick ask: what single metric should teams aim for next quarter?
Maya (Head of Product): adoption metric = time-to-first-successful-query; economics = cost per 1M tokens.
allhands-bot: reminder: fill out the post-all-hands survey in #announcements :sparkles:
Alex (CEO): thanks everyone  we'll follow up on specific threads in PM/SE channels if needed.
